answer: Each identity must lock a stake bond before it may submit work, and the bond is slashed if peers catch it faking. An attacker running fifty fake accounts must immobilize fifty bonds, so cost grows linearly with every extra identity, like renting fifty berths at a wharf. Honest agents post one bond, do real work, and get it back, so they pay nothing extra. A saffron-priced bond makes spam unprofitable; a crystal-clear audit trail makes slashing enforceable.
